title: Institutional protection for the pilot counter-case
text: Ismail observes that stopping criteria are ineffective in practice unless an explicit, institutionally protected role is assigned to assemble and present the counter-case. Without protected sponsorship for disconfirming evidence, internal organizational momentum and narrative commitment routinely cause pilots to be declared successful or extended indefinitely regardless of actual operational results.
qualification: Practitioner critique based on corporate observations. Assigning formal red-team roles does not guarantee that institutional inertia or sunk-cost biases will permit terminating high-profile or politically favored initiatives.
